analysis: Isoniazid (INH) is an antibiotic commonly used in the treatment of tuberculosis. A known side effect of INH is peripheral neuropathy, which occurs due to its interference with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) metabolism. This interference can lead to a deficiency in pyridoxine, which is essential for nerve function. The standard medical treatment for INH-induced neuropathy is supplementation with pyridoxine. This approach is well-supported by medical consensus, as it directly addresses the underlying cause of the neuropathy by replenishing the depleted vitamin B6 levels. Other vitamins such as thiamine, niacin, and riboflavin are not directly involved in the mechanism of INH-induced neuropathy, making pyridoxine the most appropriate treatment option.
